corpusSummary: An international 2026 corpus of social-science work on large language models spans human–AI interaction, AI-as-research-tool, health, education, and climate. It shifts from descriptive AI-behavior accounts toward evaluative frameworks on trust, equity, governance, safety, and ethics, with growing emphasis on AI-enabled pedagogy, responsible research practices, and real-world deployment in organizations and policy.

themes.name: Trust, adoption, and human–AI interaction
themes.description: Across domains, studies identify how presentation, privacy, peer influence, and perceived humanness shape trust, acceptance, and use of AI in counseling, education, parenting, and crisis settings.

themes.name: AI as a research tool: methods, validation, and governance
themes.description: Papers explore LLM-assisted content analysis, policy research, social simulations, and methodological frameworks, highlighting validation, transparency, and ethical oversight.

themes.name: Equity, fairness, and cultural adequacy in AI outputs
themes.description: Research assesses bias, fairness, accessibility, and cultural sensitivity in AI-generated content and tools across health, education, and information domains.

themes.name: AI-enhanced education and AI literacy
themes.description: A body of work investigates AI tutors, scaffolding, learning analytics, and literacy programs for diverse learners, including older adults, with attention to risks like overreliance.
